topStories.headline: Safeway Lawsuit Takes a Strange Turn: Developer Dropped, City and PG&E Left Holding the Case
topStories.dek: Opponents of the Marina Safeway redevelopment amended their federal complaint to remove developer Align Real Estate, leaving the City of San Francisco and PG&E as the remaining defendants — a move legal observers are calling a tactical gamble.
topStories.body:
Five days after San Francisco's Planning Department granted final approval to the 848-unit Marina Safeway redevelopment on November 6, the plaintiffs — YesAnd Foundation, Neighborhoods United SF, and four Marina District residents — filed a first amended complaint in federal court. The revised filing removed developer Align Real Estate and parent company Albertsons from the suit, leaving the City and PG&E as the surviving defendants. As the case now stands, Align can either sit on the sidelines or ask the court for permission to intervene to defend its own project.

The amended complaint still seeks to have the city's approval set aside. Plaintiffs argue that San Francisco granted final approval on November 6 without imposing conditions sufficient to address hazardous waste contamination on the site — a PG&E-adjacent parcel with a documented history of toxic materials. The complaint also points out that the city's own Property Information Map still listed the project as "under review" on November 10, four days after the approval was finalized. Additionally, plaintiffs contend that the existing 1959 Safeway building, designed by architect William Wurster, has been listed on the Register of Historical Resources since 2015 and deserves historic review.

The case is before U.S. District Court Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín. Last month Align filed a motion to dismiss the due-process claims, arguing that opponents have no constitutional right to a public hearing on a project approved under California's AB 2011 streamlining law. That motion is scheduled to be heard in February.

The 48 Hills news site, writing on November 12, framed the case as a significant test of the state's fast-track housing approval framework championed by state Senator Scott Wiener. Federal courts can move slowly, observers note, meaning the developer could potentially begin demolition and excavation work before any ruling comes down. No construction start date has been announced; the project must still obtain separate demolition and excavation permits.

topStories.headline: Magic Theatre's World Premiere of 'a Rashomon' Is Now Playing at Fort Mason
topStories.dek: Ashley Smiley's new play, conceived by Joan Osato and inspired by Akira Kurosawa's film, opened November 18 at Fort Mason and runs through December 6.
topStories.body:
Magic Theatre's world premiere production of 'a Rashomon,' written by Ashley Smiley and conceived by Joan Osato, opened Wednesday, November 18 at Fort Mason Center's Landmark Building D and plays through Sunday, December 6. Director Edris Cooper-Anifowoshe leads a cast that includes Juan Amador, Nora el Samahy, Britney Frazier, and Jeuneé Simon.

The play transplants the fractured, multiple-perspective storytelling of Kurosawa's classic 1950 film to San Francisco's own streets, setting the central mystery at Market Street near the cable-car turnaround. The production incorporates a diorama of the city, puppets, and original videography to layer its competing narratives. At the heart of the story is the anonymous death of a Black star dancer — a native son of the city — and the conflicting accounts of those who witnessed it.

Magic Theatre has operated out of Fort Mason since 1977 and is one of the few American theater companies still dedicated exclusively to new plays. The company was founded in 1967 and holds Legacy Business status with the City of San Francisco. 'a Rashomon' is the first of three productions in the company's fall 2026 season.

topStories.headline: Sherrill Now Holds Full Four-Year District 2 Mandate — What Comes Next
topStories.dek: With his November 3 re-election certified, Supervisor Stephen Sherrill enters his first full term representing the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights with the Safeway fight as his most immediate test.
topStories.body:
Supervisor Stephen Sherrill was re-elected to a full four-year term on November 3, 2026, extending a tenure that began when he won a special election for District 2 on June 2 of this year. The district covers the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights neighborhoods.

Sherrill heads into that term with the Marina Safeway redevelopment already dominating neighborhood politics. He and some residents had challenged the project's eligibility for state streamlining under AB 2011, arguing the city had misinterpreted the law — a position the Planning Department rejected before granting final approval on November 6. The federal lawsuit filed by YesAnd Foundation and neighbors is proceeding independently of the supervisor's office, but it broadly echoes the concerns Sherrill raised during the approval process.

Beyond the Safeway dispute, the new term gives Sherrill a fresh electoral mandate going into 2027 budget negotiations and any further planning decisions affecting some of San Francisco's most expensive and closely watched residential blocks.

moreNews.headline: 48 Hills: Marina Safeway Case Is a Test of California's Fast-Track Housing Law
moreNews.body: A November 12 analysis in 48 Hills argues that the federal lawsuit seeking to block the Marina Safeway redevelopment has implications well beyond one Marina District grocery store. The piece frames the case as a significant early challenge to the AB 2011 streamlining framework — the state law that allowed San Francisco to approve the 848-unit project without a public hearing and above the site's local 40-foot height limit. The plaintiffs include the YesAnd Foundation, Neighborhoods United SF, and four Marina residents; the developer Align Real Estate was dropped from the amended complaint on November 13, leaving the city and PG&E as defendants. A hearing on the motion to dismiss is scheduled for February before U.S. District Court Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín.

moreNews.headline: Haines Gallery at Fort Mason Opens '250 Years, Indigenous Futures' Exhibition
moreNews.body: Fort Mason Center's Haines Gallery is currently showing '250 Years, Indigenous Futures,' an exhibition listed on the Fort Mason campus calendar as of this week. The show is part of Fort Mason's ongoing fall 2026 visual arts programming at the waterfront campus. Specific opening and closing dates were not listed on the Fort Mason website as of this edition; visitors should check fortmason.org for current hours and admission details.
